sections.commitments:
- **License:** bindings, the provider, integration guides, reference integrations and adapters are released under an OSI-approved open-source license. 
- **Maintenance:** corpus.core maintains the bindings and the integration toolkit after the grant, funded by commercial products built on the open core. 
- **Pinned targets:** at least 12 new production integrations, at least 5 of them from the list in the first adoption milestone or protocols securing over $100 million onchain, across at least 3 application categories.
- **Exception requested:** a merged upstream pull request counts toward the integration target when the integrating team's own release schedule delays production use.
sections.in_scope:
- Production Go binding plus one additional binding only when required by a committed integration target; avoid building bindings without an adoption path.
- An EIP-1193-compatible provider and integration guides, so a wallet or dApp switches from a trusted RPC to verified reads by replacing its provider. 
- Reference integrations for a wallet and a DeFi frontend. 
- An integration program that identifies teams at wallets, DeFi protocols and other dApps, onboards them and supports each integration until it runs in production. 
- Reusable adapters and fixes from recurring integration work, published upstream.
sections.out_scope:
- Bridges and new chain integrations. A companion initiative covers them. 
- Pragmatic Adaptive Privacy (PAP). A companion initiative covers it. 
- Transaction simulation and transaction-security warnings in signing interfaces. A companion initiative covers them. 
- Commercial vRPC, prover services, and integration work for RPC providers. 
- Bindings needed only by one commercial customer or a proprietary environment.

sections.why: The security boundary of a wallet or dApp does not end at key custody. Applications continuously make security-relevant decisions from RPC data: balances, allowances, bytecode, storage, logs, name resolution and eth_call results. If those reads are manipulated, the application can display false state, route funds incorrectly or construct a transaction from a false premise. colibri replaces the RPC provider as a source of truth with locally verified proofs. Manipulated reads are a proven attack path: in April 2026, compromised RPC infrastructure (https://www.corpuscore.tech/blog/the-code-was-fine-thats-the-problem) fed false chain data to KelpDAO's bridge verifier and released about $292 million (https://unchainedcrypto.com/layerzero-links-292-million-kelp-dao-bridge-exploit-to-north-koreas-lazarus-group/). Every wallet that trusts its RPC provider depends on the same kind of infrastructure.
sections.why_grant: colibri has been in production since November 2025. Bindings are available for JavaScript/TypeScript, Swift, Kotlin/Java, Python, Dart/Flutter and Rust, and four products already run it: the Ethereum Foundation's Kohaku wallet SDK, Ambire, Freedom Browser, where it is the default verification layer, and beel.com. Those integrations are the template for this program. This grant pays for the Go binding, a drop-in provider, the integration guides and the integrations themselves. A team starting from scratch would first have to build the client and the existing bindings.

initiative.summary: A wallet can protect keys perfectly and still show a user false blockchain state. This grant moves colibri's local cryptographic verification into production wallets, DeFi frontends and other Web3 applications, so balances, allowances, contract state, logs and calls are verified before an application acts on them. It funds a Go binding, a drop-in provider and at least 12 new production integrations across at least 3 application categories.
initiative.title: colibri: Make dApps Verify What They Show in Wallets, DeFi and Web3 Apps
